messages:
amira: Quick sync — I ran the first onboarding sweep for bobcat-embed (13B) w/ fp16 vs int8 (post-training static quant) on the semantic-suite benchmark. High-level: recall@1 down ~0.9% vs fp16, recall@5 basically unchanged. Putting raw numbers below and a short note about clusters/tail behavior.

sanjay: Nice, can you paste the exact metrics? Also which seeds / eval split?

amira: Sure — eval split = semantic-suite v2 (50k queries), seeds = 42/43 (two runs). Results (median over 3 runs):

```
Model         recall@1    recall@5    avg_cos_sim
bobcat:fp16   0.872       0.953       0.412
bobcat:int8   0.863       0.951       0.409
delta         -0.009      -0.002      -0.003
```

Notes: per-query latency improved ~12% at batch=16, throughput ~x1.25.

marco: Do you see the drop concentrated on any particular cohorts? short queries / multilingual / low-frequency tokens?

amira: Yep — looked at cohort breakdown. Main hit on short queries (<8 tokens) and rare-entity queries. For head queries recall@1 almost identical. I also inspected embedding norms and cosine histograms — int8 a tiny bit more compressed in magnitude (avg norm -1.8%).

lina: Can you attach the UMAPs or a quick diff image? I want to eyeball cluster bleed for the tail.

amira: Uploaded two quick UMAP snapshots to the shared drive (link: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/bobcat-embed/4299991111-umap.png). Observations: tail cluster centroids move closer to nearby unrelated clusters, especially in the 'legal' / 'finance' micro-cohort — visual overlap increased.

marco: That matches the recall hit. Might be quantization scale / per-channel mismatch. Did you try per-channel int8 or clamp tweaks?

amira: Not yet. I ran symmetric per-tensor int8 with linear calibration. Next steps I plan: 1) run per-channel int8, 2) try 4-bit mixed (int4 on activations where safe), 3) run a focused holdout on short queries with 10k queries to get a stable signal.

sanjay: Also try enabling per-layer clamp on attention outputs — we saw similar tail effects in the lark bring-up. If per-channel fixes it with <0.5% recall@1 drop, it's a win.

amira: Agreed. I'll kick off the per-channel sweep. Ops: can we reserve 4x A100-dedicated for a 6h window this afternoon? Prefer dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor variance. @ops-bot /cc @lina

ops-bot: Reservation confirmed — 4x A100 reserved on cluster "dedicated-ml-2" from 17:30 to 23:30 UTC. Job quota assigned to amira (job-id: rbw-8723). :white_check_mark:

amira: Thanks! I'll post results here once the sweep finishes. If per-channel closes the gap, I'll follow up with a small-canary rollout to staging and a stronger eval on multilingual holdouts.

lina: If you get a promising per-channel config, also run the silhouette/cohesion metric (k=5) and a recall@1 on the short-query holdout before any rollout.

amira: Will do. TL;DR: int8 gives good latency wins, small recall@1 degradation concentrated on short/rare queries — next: per-channel + clamp sweep, dedicated GPUs reserved, will report back with updated metrics + UMAP diffs. :rocket:
